context_title: best open weight llm model today

entries.query: best open weight llm model today
entries.answer:
The best openweight LLM today depends on what you mean by “best,” but the strongest allaround answer from current public rankings is GLM5.2, which appears at the top of a live opensource leaderboard with a Quality Index of 51.1.[1]

 Best overall
If you want a single pick for broad capability, GLM5.2 is the most defensible “best openweight model today” from the ranking I found, and it is also described as the strongest codingoriented model on that page.[1]

 Strong alternatives
For longcontext, agentic, or codingheavy work, Kimi K2.6 is presented by recent coverage as one of the strongest openweight options, especially for longhorizon coding and autonomous workflows.[2][3]

If you care more about general benchmark prestige and largescale capability, Llama 4 Maverick, DeepSeek V4, and Qwen3 235B are also repeatedly mentioned among the top openweight models in recent 2026 roundups.[4][5][6][7]

 Practical choice
For most users, the real answer is not just “which model is best,” but “which model fits my hardware and task.” A toptier model like GLM5.2 or Kimi K2.6 may be excellent on paper, while a smaller model can be better if you need something you can actually run locally.[5][8]

 Recommendation
For a simple oneline recommendation: GLM5.2 for best overall quality, Kimi K2.6 for coding/agentic work, and Qwen3 or Llama 4 if you want a widely discussed alternative ecosystem.[7][4][2][5]
